title: Anthropic IPO prospectus reveals surging costs, $42B 2025 net loss
content:
Anthropic IPO prospectus reveals surging costs, $42B 2025 net loss: report
Anthropic ANTHROPIC reported a net loss of $42 billion in 2025, and plans to spend $518 billion on cloud, computing and infrastructure obligations in coming years, according to its IPO prospectus seen by Reuters.
The prospectus details how the company has grown sharply in the last year — while also posting wider losses. Revenue grew 12-fold in 2025 to nearly $4.6 billion, even as the company lost more than $8 billion on an operating basis, excluding writedowns of various liabilities mostly tied to previous fundraising, the report said, citing documents.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has called for the global AI community to slow the pace of releasing new capabilities to address those concerns. Still, Anthropic rolled out its new Opus 5.5 model last week to counter OpenAI’s momentum since its launch of GPT-6 Astra, ahead of its own expected IPO.
The AI lab spent $7.33 billion on compute and infrastructure last year, a threefold surge from 2024, accounting for more than half of its $12.65 billion in total operating expenses, the report said.
Anthropic had cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments totaling $20.28 billion as of December 31, the prospectus shows. Anthropic's debut would follow SpaceX's IPO that valued Elon Musk's company at $1.77 trillion.
Anthropic's biggest challenger remains OpenAI OPENAI, which confidentially filed for an IPO in June. The ChatGPT maker is expected to list by early 2027, according to media reports.
Anthropic competes with OpenAI, SpaceX’s SPCX xAI, Alphabet’s Google GOOG GOOGL and Meta META in AI.

report.summary: Anthropic’s IPO prospectus shows 2025 revenue surged to $4.6B but net loss hit $42B, with $518B in future cloud and infrastructure commitments.
report.background: Anthropic, founded by former OpenAI researchers, has become a leading AI lab behind the Claude model family. The company is preparing for an IPO amid an intense arms race with OpenAI, Google, Meta and xAI. The prospectus arrives as AI labs spend heavily on chips, data centers and cloud capacity to train and serve frontier models. While Anthropic’s revenue grew rapidly, its costs and losses also ballooned, reflecting the capital-intensive nature of frontier AI. The filing follows SpaceX’s IPO and precedes an expected OpenAI listing, setting up a major test of public-market appetite for AI companies.
key_points: Anthropic’s 2025 revenue grew 12-fold to nearly $4.6 billion, but its operating loss exceeded $8 billion before certain writedowns, and its net loss reached $42 billion, according to the IPO prospectus.
Compute and infrastructure spending hit $7.33 billion last year, a threefold increase from 2024, accounting for more than half of Anthropic’s $12.65 billion in total operating expenses.
The company plans $518 billion in future cloud, computing and infrastructure obligations, while holding $20.28 billion in cash, equivalents and short-term investments as of December 31.
Anthropic’s IPO would follow SpaceX’s listing, which valued Elon Musk’s company at $1.77 trillion. OpenAI confidentially filed for an IPO in June and is expected to list by early 2027.

Anthropic released its Opus 5.5 model last week to counter OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra momentum. CEO Dario Amodei has simultaneously called for slowing the release of new AI capabilities over safety concerns.
report.impact: The prospectus exposes the extreme economics of frontier AI: explosive revenue growth paired with enormous compute bills and losses. For the AI industry, it raises pressure to prove that massive infrastructure spending can eventually yield sustainable profits. Developers may see model access improve, but API pricing, rate limits and enterprise terms could tighten as labs pass on compute costs. Regular users may get more capable assistants, yet subscriptions could rise and market consolidation may reduce choice. Investors will scrutinize Anthropic’s IPO as a bellwether for AI valuations, especially with OpenAI expected to follow.
report.tools: To follow the story, monitor SEC EDGAR for Anthropic and OpenAI IPO filings, plus Reuters, TradingView and Seeking Alpha for coverage. For hands-on testing, try Anthropic’s Claude/Opus models, OpenAI’s GPT APIs, and open-source alternatives like Llama, Mistral, Ollama and vLLM. Cloud cost tools such as Infracost and OpenCost can help developers understand the infrastructure economics behind these AI labs.
